definitions.explanation: A processed seafood product made from white fish paste that is shaped and steamed. A staple ingredient in Japanese cuisine.

examples.japanese: かまぼこを{薄|うす}く{切|き}る。
ラーメンにかまぼこが{乗|の}っている。
examples.english: There's kamaboko on top of the ramen.

examples.japanese: おせち{料理|りょうり}には{紅白|こうはく}のかまぼこが{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Red and white kamaboko are essential in New Year's dishes.

notes:
Also written as {蒲鉾|かまぼこ}. Made from surimi ({擂|す}り{身|み}), a paste of minced white fish.

VARIETIES:
- {板|いた}かまぼこ: standard half-moon shaped kamaboko on a wooden board
- {笹|ささ}かまぼこ: leaf-shaped kamaboko (specialty of {仙台|せんだい})
- なると: spiral-patterned kamaboko used in ramen
- {紅白|こうはく}かまぼこ: red and white kamaboko for celebrations

CULTURE: {紅白|こうはく}かまぼこ (red and white kamaboko) is a traditional part of おせち{料理|りょうり} (New Year's dishes). The half-moon shape is said to resemble the first sunrise of the year.
